extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors reporting in vivo animal experiments; peer reviewers and journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to report design, conduct, analysis, and resources for in vivo animal experiments to ensure reproducibility, transparency, and validity of manuscripts and registered reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome measure specification and protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly identify the primary outcome measure and state whether it was defined as such prior to data collection and whether it was used in the sample size calculation. If there was no primary outcome measure, explicitly state so. Registering a protocol in advance protects against selective outcome reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register a protocol in advance to avoid selective outcome reporting (p-hacking). Studies that claim to test a hypothesis but do not specify a pre-defined primary outcome, or change the primary outcome after data collection (primary outcome switching), risk selective reporting of statistically significant results. See item 19 – Protocol registration. Examples: (quoted example texts showing clear primary/secondary outcome statements and power calculations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis (7a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods in enough detail that another researcher could re-analyse the raw data and obtain the same results. Make clear which method was used for which analysis. Both exploratory and hypothesis-testing studies should report appropriate descriptive and/or inferential statistics. Analysing data using different methods and selectively reporting those with statistically significant results constitutes p-hacking. Relevant information to describe the statistical methods include the items listed in separate rubrics (outcome measures, independent variables, nuisance variables, handling missing values, multiple comparisons, software/code). For bespoke analyses, describe the analysis pipeline (starting model and model simplification steps). Refer to SAMPL guidelines for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report the outcome measures used in each analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state the outcome measures used in each analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome measures may be affected by treatments and by biological/technical factors (sex, litter, age, weight, cage, time of day, batch, experimenter). Describe which outcome was analysed and how it was measured so readers can judge appropriateness. When reporting descriptive statistics, state which measure of central tendency (mean/median) and variability (SD, range, IQR) are used and any modifications made to raw data (e.g. relative quantification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report independent variables and nuisance variables included in analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: List the independent variables of interest and the nuisance variables taken into account in each statistical test (e.g. blocking factors or covariates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce bias and account for variability, include biological and technical factors (sex, litter, cage, batch, experimenter) in design and analysis, e.g. as blocking factors or covariates. Describe how such factors were handled in both design (randomisation, blocking) and analysis (including them in the model or aggregating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe how hierarchical/clustered data were handled
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise the hierarchy that can exist in an experiment (e.g. cage, litter, animal, cells from same animal) and describe measures taken in analysis/design to account for clustering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clustering can make outcomes for units within the same cluster more similar. Manage clustering by including cluster effects in the model or by aggregating outcome measures to the appropriate hierarchical level (cage/litter/animal). Describe the data hierarchy and measures taken to account for it when assessing appropriateness of statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report what statistical analyses were performed and references for methods
rubrics_metrics.description: State precisely what statistical analyses were performed and provide references for the methods used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it clear which test or model was applied to which data. For bespoke analyses (e.g. complex regressions), detail the analysis pipeline, starting model and any simplification steps. Cite methodological references where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report how missing values were handled
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how missing values were handled in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any imputation or exclusion rules, how many values were missing per variable/group, and the rationale for the chosen approach. Transparency about missing data handling is essential for assessing validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report adjustment for multiple comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any adjustment made for multiple comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple tests were conducted, report procedures to control false positives (e.g. Bonferroni, FDR) or rationale for not adjusting. Selective reporting of unadjusted significant tests introduces bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report software package, version, and code used for analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: State the software package and version used, and provide computer code if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing software and code improves reproducibility. Cite packages and versions, and share scripts or analysis code (e.g. as supplementary files or repositories). See SAMPL and reproducible code guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report all analyses performed; avoid selective reporting/p-hacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Report all analyses performed in full and avoid selectively reporting only significant analyses (p-hacking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysing the data using different methods and selectively reporting those with statistically significant results constitutes p-hacking and introduces bias. Registering analysis plans/protocols in advance helps protect against selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methods used to assess statistical assumptions and actions if unmet (7b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach, and what was done if the assumptions were not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the type of outcome measure and methods used to test assumptions (e.g. Shapiro–Wilk for normality, Levene's test for homogeneity). Use visual plots where appropriate. If assumptions are violated, report transformations (log, sqrt) or alternative tests (non-parametric) used. If assumptions were not tested, state this explicitly. Give specific information about which transformation was applied to which outcome measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reporting descriptive statistics, state measures of central tendency and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting descriptive statistics, explicitly state which measure of central tendency (mean or median) and which measure of variability (SD, range, quartiles or IQR) are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about reported summary statistics and any back-transformations applied for visualization. This aids correct interpretation and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide species-appropriate details of experimental animals (8a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide species-appropriate details of the animals used, including species, strain and substrain, sex, age or developmental stage, and, if relevant, weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These characteristics influence experimental results and are critical for internal/external validity and reproducibility. Include summary statistics for age and weight per group (e.g. mean ± SD) and, if possible, baseline values for individual animals (supplementary). If reporting sex/weight is infeasible (e.g. embryos, stressful measurements), provide justification. Precise age often more informative than vague terms like 'adult'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report provenance, health/immune status, genetic modification and genotype of animals (8b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details on provenance of animals, health/immune status, genetic modification status, genotype, and any previous procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report supplier/source, health status (SPF and pathogens tested), history of previous procedures, and for genetically modified animals describe modification (knockout/overexpression), genotype (homozygous/heterozygous), manipulated genes, methods used to generate animals, confirmation of modification, and control animals (e.g. littermate controls). Use standard nomenclature and cite resources for species-specific nomenclature. If health status unknown, state explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe experimental procedures in enough detail to allow replication (9 / 9a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental group, including controls, describe what was done, how it was done, and what was used, with enough detail to allow others to replicate procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures to develop the model, outcome measurement procedures, pre- and post-experimental procedures (animal handling, welfare monitoring, euthanasia). Provide timeline/schematic of procedures. Include quality assurance/quality control. For procedure-specific information, report items listed (e.g. for pharmacological procedures: formulation, dose, volume, route, frequency, evidence agent reaches target; for surgical procedures: anaesthesia, analgesia, aseptic techniques, monitoring; for infections: agent, dose, route, timing; for euthanasia: method and humane standards compliance). Provide details on cell lines (identification, provenance, authentication, RRID), reagents (manufacturer, catalogue/lot, purity, RRID), equipment (manufacturer, model/version, calibration, RRID). Consider sharing detailed step-by-step protocols via repositories (Protocols.io) with DOIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report timing and frequency of procedures and measurements (9b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report the frequency and timing of experimental procedures and measurements, including light/dark cycle, circadian cues, and experimental time sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing (e.g. lights on at 08:00, 12L:12D) and intervals between baseline and measurements can affect outcomes. Report timing/frequency of welfare assessments. If timing varies between animals, provide a supplementary table per animal. Examples show blood sampling times, fasting periods, repeated clamps with recovery intervals, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report where procedures occurred and acclimatisation periods (9c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe where procedures were conducted, including details of any acclimatisation periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physiological acclimatisation after stressful events (transport) allows stabilisation; durations vary by species and protocol (from 24 hours to more than a week). Report location details (transport, facility, operating theatre, lab) and duration of any acclimatisation and rationale.
